The Clavinet is an electrophonic keyboard instrument, Hornbostel–Sachs 513, belonging to the mixed keyboard, electrophonic and mechanical family. In construction, sixty tensioned steel strings lie at an angle beneath the keys; when a key is pressed, the rubber pad beneath it strikes the string and stops it at a pitch much as a guitarist's finger would, and an electromagnetic pickup turns the string's vibration into a current, so the instrument usually has to be plugged into a keyboard amplifier to sound. Playing force affects the volume, and there is an aftertouch effect as the string is stretched. It was originally for the home and later became a stage instrument, much used in rock, funk and reggae; Stevie Wonder used it heavily, above all on the 1972 track 'Superstition'.
Clavinet多數型號有60鍵，音域F1至E6。每鍵以橡膠墊敲擊張緊鋼弦，經電: Most Clavinet models have 60 keys, with a range from F1 to E6. Each key strikes a tensioned steel string with a rubber pad, and an electromagnetic pickup turns this into a current, creating an electric-guitar timbre on a keyboard; the volume is set by the preamp knob on the left and by the pickup selector, and the keyboard feels weighted because it takes the force of the strike, so the player can vary the volume key by key as on a piano or a clavichord, with an aftertouch effect as the string is pulled. Unlike the Cembalet and Pianet, which pluck metal reeds with a pad, the Clavinet sounds by striking strings.
Clavinet由恩斯特·扎卡里亞斯設計，霍納公司於1964至1982年在西德特: The Clavinet was designed by Ernst Zacharias and made by Hohner in Trossingen, West Germany, between 1964 and 1982. Zacharias joined Hohner in 1954 and, inspired by Bach's harpsichord music, developed the 1961 Claviphon prototype into a mechanical action in which rubber pads strike tensioned strings. It was at first a household instrument aimed at late medieval, Baroque and early Classical music, and later became popular for its practicality on stage, common in rock, funk and reggae; Stevie Wonder used it heavily on 'Superstition' in 1972. In the 1970s models such as the D6, E7 and Duo strengthened the tone choices and the rejection of stage noise, production stopped in 1982, and digital keyboards later imitated it, while a repair trade continues.
Clavinet的發聲體為60條張力鋼弦，以橡膠墊擊弦，弦端以紗線制音；拾音器以: The Clavinet's sounding body is 60 tensioned steel strings, struck with rubber pads and damped at the ends with yarn; the pickup is sealed in epoxy inside a plastic case. Body materials vary by model: the Clavinet I has a brown teak veneer case, a bronze front panel and wooden legs; the C has a red vinyl shell, a black aluminium panel, an acrylic music stand and steel-tube legs; the L has wooden legs and a clear plastic music stand; the D6 has black vinyl leatherette and teak veneer; the E7 has a black vinyl leatherette case and a metal lid. The rest is not stated.
演奏時將 Clavinet 接上鍵盤放大器，或依型號使用內建放大器、電源或電池。: In playing, the Clavinet is plugged into a keyboard amplifier, or, depending on the model, uses a built-in amplifier, mains power or batteries. Pressing a key makes the rubber pad beneath it strike a tensioned steel string, and the string's vibration is turned into a current by the pickup and sent out through the preamplifier. The keys are weighted, so the force of the press changes the volume, and yarn damps the string when the key is released. A beginner can start by setting the volume, the pickup selection and the tone switches, then practise a steady touch to control the length and strength of each note.
